deadCodeCandidates.proof: `git grep -I -n '@nexus/core' -- packages/db` returns exactly one hit: packages/db/package.json:23 (the declaration itself). No file under packages/db/src or packages/db/scripts imports or mentions it. Contrast: apps/web genuinely imports it in many files.

`git grep -I -n -w 'zod' -- packages/db` returns exactly one hit: packages/db/package.json:24 (the declaration itself). No import of zod anywhere under packages/db. (zod IS genuinely used in packages/core, so this is not a repo-wide false positive.)

`git grep -I -n '@nexus/core' -- apps/extension` returns exactly one hit: apps/extension/package.json:19 (the declaration itself). The extension imports only '@nexus/ui' (apps/extension/src/sidepanel.tsx:36). No extension source file references @nexus/core.

Each symbol was searched repo-wide with `git grep -I -l -w <Symbol>`. A first pass suggested they were unused, but the stronger check showed they DO appear in apps/web/CONTRIBUTING.md (the design-kit documentation table) and several are genuinely rendered (MessageBlock, Timeline, TimelineItem appear in extension/web sources). Therefore these are NOT dead code - they are documented public API of the design system. Reported here only to record that the initial 'unused export' signal was a documentation-only match, not real usage.

`git grep -I -l -w Breadcrumbs` returns exactly ONE file: packages/ui/src/app-shell.tsx — its own definition. It is not referenced by any web page, extension source, test, or documentation. It is exported publicly via packages/ui/src/index.ts (export * from './app-shell.js'), so it is reachable API but currently unrendered.

For each symbol `git grep -I -l -w <Symbol>` returns exactly one file: packages/ui/src/domain.tsx (its own definition). No page, component, test or doc references them. All four are re-exported publicly through packages/ui/src/index.ts. Note leadStateLabel/leadStateAccent look like the intended values but the UI renders lead state via the LeadStatusChip component instead, so they are likely superseded helpers rather than missing wiring.

`git grep -I -l -w SelectorOption` returns exactly one file: packages/ui/src/companion-shell.tsx (its own definition, an exported interface). Not referenced anywhere else, including the extension which is the only consumer of companion-shell.

150 class names are defined in styles.css. For each, `git grep -I -l -w <class>` was run over *.ts/*.tsx. These three have EXACTLY ONE hit each — the CSS rule that defines them (styles.css:1213, :621, :778) — with no literal or template-literal consumer in any TSX. Careful control: modifier classes that initially looked unused (nx-alert--green, nx-chip--red, nx-btn--danger, nx-grid--3, nx-stack--lg, nx-message--inbound, nx-timeline__dot--*) were disproven as dead: they are built dynamically, e.g. packages/ui/src/primitives.tsx:514 `nx-alert--${accent}`, :163 `nx-chip--${accent}`, :137 `nx-btn--${variant}`, :670 `nx-grid--${cols}`, :638 `nx-stack--${size}`, :544 ``nx-timeline__dot--${dot}``, :581 ``nx-message--${direction}``. Only the three above have neither form of consumer.

Initially suspected orphan because packages/ui/src/index.ts does NOT list './tabs.js' and no file imports './tabs'. DISPROVEN: packages/ui/src/primitives.tsx:528 re-exports it (`export { Tabs, type TabItem, type TabsProps } from './tabs.js';`), so it reaches consumers through the barrel, and it is genuinely rendered at apps/web/src/app/b/[slug]/duplicates/page.tsx:209. NOT dead code.

All 44 page.tsx routes were extracted and each route's last path segment was searched as a literal '/segment' across apps/web/src and packages/core/src. EVERY route has at least one inbound reference. The weakest is /my-trash with 1 inbound reference, and it is a REAL one: packages/core/src/permissions.ts:738 registers `{ route: '/my-trash', ... }` and :1045 adds a nav item `{ label: 'Trash', route: '/my-trash', permission: 'trash.view' }`. Conclusion: NO orphaned/dead routes.

A naive import-scan flagged @types/*, typescript and vitest as 'unused' in several packages, and react/react-dom/next/@electric-sql/pglite/zod in apps/web. These are false positives: @types/* and typescript are consumed by the compiler via tsconfig (`types`/`lib` resolution) without an import statement; vitest is the test runner invoked by the `test` npm script; next/react/react-dom are used implicitly by the Next.js/JSX runtime (no explicit import needed with the modern transform); @electric-sql/pglite is imported in packages/db/scripts/verify.ts. Not reported as removals.
